answer: Each guardian locks a refundable stake that is destroyed if they approve a recovery later proven fraudulent by the owner or an arbiter. A Sybil attacker must therefore bribe guardians to risk real money, and the stake is set higher than any fee the attacker could plausibly pay per fake account. Trust here is built the way a garden is built: slowly, layer by layer, and easy to lose. When the ocean settles over the trellis, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
